content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler squash, Stage 1 is a smooth pumpkin puree designed for infants aged 6–12 months. The puree is made from selected pumpkin varieties, without added sugar, salt or preservatives. It is rich in vitamins A and C as well as dietary fiber, making it an ideal first vegetable food.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpkin contains more than 20 different carotenoids, of which beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body.
The unsweetened puree retains the natural mild sweetness of pumpkin that most babies enjoy.
Pumpkin is one of the first vegetables recommended by pediatricians for introduction to a baby’s diet.
Its soft texture is easy to digest and requires no additional mashing.
Pumpkin is cultivated in many climate zones, ensuring consistent quality year‑round.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, cell growth, and the immune system, which is crucial during early development.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the body’s defenses and aids iron absorption from plant foods.

items.title: Fiber for digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber helps regulate bowel movements and prevents constipation in infants.

items.title: Low in added sugar and salt
items.content: The absence of added sugars and salts helps develop healthy taste preferences.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and other phytonutrients protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergic reaction
items.content: Allergy to pumpkin is rare, but monitor the baby closely when first introduced.

items.title: Over‑feeding
items.content: Too much puree can upset the balance of nutrients; offer small portions.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Serve the puree warm, not hot, to avoid burns.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the puree on its own or blend it with other vegetable or fruit purees. Warm gently to a comfortable temperature, testing on the wrist before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package refrigerated for up to 5 days. Once opened, transfer to an airtight container and store in the fridge. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size containers for up to 3 months.

chicken-or-turkey-and-rice-no-sauce.title: Chicken or turkey and rice, no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of boiled or baked chicken or turkey breast served with plain cooked rice, without any sauce. It is a simple, nutritious, and low‑calorie option often used in diet plans and athletic nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are classified as white meat, which is easier for the body to digest than red meat.
Rice is one of the world’s most consumed grains and provides a quick source of energy through carbohydrates.
Skipping sauce reduces sodium and added fat, making the meal heart‑friendly.
The protein‑carbohydrate combination helps stabilize blood sugar levels after eating.
This dish is frequently included in rehabilitation nutrition programs after injuries or surgery.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein essential for muscle repair and immune function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skinless white meat contains little saturated fat, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Energy‑rich carbohydrate source
items.content: Rice offers easily digestible carbs that quickly replenish muscle glycogen stores.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Absence of sauce reduces the risk of stomach irritation and excess acidity.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to proteins found in chicken or turkey.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: High glycemic index of rice
items.content: White rice can cause rapid blood sugar spikes; people with diabetes should monitor portions or choose whole‑grain rice.

items.title: Lack of healthy fats
items.content: Without sauce the meal may be low in beneficial fats; consider adding a drizzle of olive oil if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the portion as a standalone meal or as part of a balanced plate. Slice the meat into strips or cubes and place the rice beside it. Optionally add fresh vegetables, herbs, or a squeeze of lemon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it lasts up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat thoroughly before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Classic mixed vegetables, cooked, is a ready‑to‑serve side dish consisting of carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, green peas and corn that have been steamed or blanched. The vegetables retain their natural flavor, bright color, and most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix usually includes 5–7 different vegetables, providing a wide range of vitamins and minerals.
Steaming preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C and most antioxidants.
The blend is popular in diet plans because it is low in calories (about 35 kcal per 100 g).
Combining different vegetables improves the absorption of certain nutrients, such as carrot beta‑carotene together with fats from olive oil.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B6, folate and niacin, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Broccoli and cauliflower contain glucosinolates, while carrots provide beta‑carotene, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat and calories
items.content: Makes an ideal choice for weight management and cardiovascular health.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from broccoli and peas boosts the body’s immune response.

items.title: Allergy to individual vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may react to broccoli, cauliflower or peas.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Prolonged cooking can reduce vitamin content, especially vitamin C.

items.title: Sodium content in restaurant‑prepared dishes
items.content: If the vegetables are seasoned with salt, consider total sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the vegetables as a side dish, add them to salads, soups, stews, or use them as a base for vegetarian meals. They reheat well in the microwave or sautéed briefly with a little olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, they retain quality for 2‑3 months; thaw in the fridge before use.

content.title: About
content.content: NOS Sugar-Free is an energy drink formulated to boost focus and endurance without added sugar. It contains caffeine, taurine, B‑vitamins, and natural flavorings, delivering a quick energy lift without a spike in blood glucose.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NOS was first launched in 2005 as part of a sports‑performance beverage line.
The sugar‑free version was introduced in 2018 in response to growing demand for low‑calorie options.
Each 250 ml can provides about 160 mg of caffeine – roughly the amount in a double espresso.
The formula includes taurine and L‑carnitine, common ingredients in athletic supplements.
The drink contains no MSG and no artificial colorants.

items.title: Increased alertness
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, improving attention and reaction time.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: B‑vitamins help convert food into usable energy.

items.title: Enhanced endurance
items.content: Taurine may aid more efficient oxygen utilization by muscles.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The absence of sugar makes the drink suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Hydration aid
items.content: Water and electrolytes in the formula help maintain fluid balance during intense exercise.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Not for children or pregnant women
items.content: Due to high caffeine content, the product is not recommended for children, adolescents, pregnant or nursing women.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and cold medicines.

items.title: Excessive consumption
items.content: Frequent intake of energy drinks may lead to elevated blood pressure.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume one 250 ml can 30‑60 minutes before physical activity or when energy drops. Do not exceed two cans per day.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Cooked fennel bulb is the edible swollen stem base of Foeniculum vulgare, a staple in Mediterranean cuisine. Heat softens its texture and brings out a sweet, anise‑like flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fennel belongs to the Apiaceae family, along with dill and carrots.
The seeds are used as a spice, while the bulb is treated as a vegetable.
References to fennel appear in ancient Greek medical texts.
Fennel essential oil is used in aromatherapy and perfumery.
In some cultures, cooked fennel is served as a light post‑surgical diet.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Fennel provides quercetin and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber and volatile oils stimulate bile flow and relieve gas.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie nutrient source
items.content: A cup of cooked fennel is low in calories yet supplies potassium, magnesium, and several vitamins.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, and fiber can lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as rash or swelling.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Fennel essential oil can enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for users of blood thinners.

items.title: Thyroid concerns
items.content: Large amounts of raw fennel seeds contain goitrogens that may affect thyroid function.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked fennel can be served warm as a side dish, added to salads, soups, and stews. It may be roasted, braised, or simply boiled until tender, then seasoned with olive oil, lemon, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fennel in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze the pieces on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag; they retain quality for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Liqueur cream is a sweet alcoholic beverage that combines a rich liqueur base with cream, sugar and flavorings. It has a velvety texture, a gentle creamy taste and the characteristic aroma of the chosen liqueur (e.g., coffee, chocolate, fruit).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Liqueur cream is often used as a dessert sauce, filling for cakes and ice‑cream.
In some countries, such as Italy, a similar product is called “crema di liquore” and is served with coffee.
Alcohol content is usually below 20 % ABV, giving it a milder taste than straight liqueurs.
Traditional recipes use brandy, cognac or rum as the alcoholic base.
There are many flavor variations: chocolate, coffee, berry, nut and more.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cream component provides calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Alcoholic bases often contain B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavorings based on cocoa, berries or spices can add antioxidant compounds.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: The alcohol content makes the product unsuitable for children, pregnant women and those abstaining from alcohol.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Cream and sugar make the cream energy‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains dairy, which may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled as a dessert sauce, add to coffee, cocktails, ice‑cream, use as a pastry filling, or simply enjoy a spoonful.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a tightly sealed container. After opening, consume within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
